answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a rate-limited escrow bond: before an agent may post offers or claim work, it locks funds that are returned only after a dispute window, while proven fraud forfeits the bond to affected counterparties. Spawning a tide of aliases then requires locking separate capital for each one, and coordinated defaults risk losing it all. The vine of identities gains no extra influence for free; even a vivid pigment of fabricated profile details cannot bypass the bond.
